hypothesis: Validation-only repair for bounded noncanonical integer-controlled reduction fission whose ordinary vectorized consumer reuses integer arithmetic with fewer nowrap flags or materializes an equivalent completed-count expression. The LLVM transformation, admission policy, original corpus and profitability model are unchanged. The checker should advance beyond affine_runtime without accepting changed producer arithmetic, weaker controls or storage bounds as completed counts.
semantics: The original instruction must still appear as a complete instruction in its original block, with exact opcode, scalar type, ordered operands, predicates and successors (apart from the existing latch-exit redirection and relocated reduction state). The only additional instruction relation is one-way removal of nuw/nsw from parsed scalar add/sub/mul/shl: the operation, result and operands must match; flags may be a subset only; constants must fit the integer width and the recognized shl uses a constant in-range shift. Removal replaces poison with a wrapping result and leaves every originally defined execution unchanged. Added flags, other arithmetic changes, exact/disjoint changes and FP relaxation are rejected. The checker also rejects all FP fast-math flags in the affine function. Per-instruction metadata handling, exact membership, prefix/comment/split-line and placement checks are retained. Unique SSA definitions are required, and the ordinal, increment and single-input completed export are now checked as complete definitions in their actual blocks. Permission to use n no longer depends on a function-name suffix. It requires a small structural certificate for the original i64 control: the dominating unsigned 1<=n<=65 entry guard, an acyclic forward producer CFG with one exiting latch and exact preserved edges, the original IV/start/step/limit/compare/branch definitions, and bounded origins for relational controls. These prove actual completed N=n. Only then may the checker accept n or a checked chain of observed SSA definitions. For affine_runtime and the equality wrap analogue, span=2*n in [2,130] gives ((span-2) lshr 1)+1=n, including n=1; add span,-2 and sub span,2 are the two explicit spellings. The same retained module already shows five other narrow chains, so explicit templates and short algebraic proofs cover its unsigned umin/udiv, signed smax, signed descending smin, current-IV and enclosing-row counts. Every chain operand, width, operation/flag subset, constant, defining block and order is checked; there is no arbitrary SSA acceptance or solver. The enclosing certificate additionally checks rows in [1,4], the zero-based row recurrence and its edges; its two-block hoisted chain is checked in outer.ph then outer. Relational modular early-exit siblings lack these certificates and must consume the actual ordinal increment or a verified single-input latch export, even when renamed. Compaction continues through the unchanged check_compact_count proof of P, its counter/merge/export/control linkage and P=0 bypass with unchanged starts. Executable validation remains the existing real-opt one/two-LV matrix against original scalar IR and independent C formulas, with exact header/latch/participant/vector/tail probes, null zero-entry and inactive operands, all P=0..65, aliases, future-row reuse, canaries, ordered FP bits/signed zeros and capacity boundaries.
costs: No LLVM compiler code or C execution harness is changed. This validation repair adds no target allocation, scratch traffic, reread, recomputation, duplicated producer operation, guard or compiler analysis. The checker adds per-function SSA maps, constant-size control/expansion templates and small CFG scans; instruction preservation keeps normalized sets with an O(1) same-SSA lookup for the exceptional flag-removal comparison. Its bounded fixture recognizer is not a general algebra/SMT solver, enumerator or profitability model. The retained 14-function input affects only validation and is never assembled as an executable reference. Underlying costs are unchanged: noncanonical producers have a private ordinal and nuw increment plus completed export; compact producers count only participants and retain an empty-stream guard. Capacity M times unique contribution allocation sizes plus padding is entry allocated, capped by the existing 65536-byte per-candidate limit and signed pointer-index ceiling. At M=65 mixed fixtures reserve 1044 accounted bytes (65*i32+65*double+65*float with 4 padding bytes), with 16*N logical bytes of stores and 16*N loads, or 16*P each for compaction. Enclosing rows reuse 784 accounted bytes (65*i32+65*double with padding), with 12*N stores and 12*N loads per row, without multiplying storage by rows. Scalar capacity fixtures reserve 4/1020/65536 bytes at 1/255/16384 i32 contributions and transfer 8*N bytes total, including 131072 bytes at the full ceiling. There are no original-input rereads, contribution recomputation, mask arrays, new versioning checks, dynamic allocations or unbounded storage. The compiler's existing finite affine witness/range proof and CFG/dependence scans are untouched. Physical stack traffic, register pressure, RVV execution and performance remain unmeasured.
limitations: The worker ran no compiler (including host compilation), build, lit RUN, VectorizeTests, execution checker, test runner or try.sh. Only read-only artifact/source/JSON inspection and source/report editing were performed. No fresh validation result exists. The retained EVL fixture and source-derived compiler-path diagnosis are not fresh execution or an instrumented compiler trace. The t000025 harness compiled successfully and passed 44 lit files and 99 VectorizeTests, but execution validation failed at affine_runtime's removed shl flags before complete comparisons, affine RVV verification or primary corpus evaluation. This change intentionally recognizes only the demonstrated i64 guard/control/SSA shapes; arbitrary equivalent arithmetic, alternative guard constants (even a smaller safe bound), arbitrary forwarding/hoisting and unobserved LV2/scalar-tail forms are not accepted. A later failure requires retained IR and a narrow repair, not relaxed provenance. Inherited compiler limitations include unsupported non-affine/pointer/FP controls, arbitrary non-strict/non-lattice certificates, unbounded or unrepresentable counts, oversized untiled per-candidate scratch, producer cycles/extra recurrences, unsupported effects/live-outs/calls, independent participation streams and strictfp/constrained FP. Strict and explicitly enabled fission FP reordering remain separate contracts without added fast-math or errno assumptions. Host fixed-vscale scalar-remainder execution is not EVL/VP host execution, RVV target execution or a speedup measurement; RVV machine verification is code generation only. No direction maturity, newly selected original benchmarks or performance improvement is claimed. No benchmarks, harness, other worktrees, binaries, Git index/history/refs or unfinished d2 work were modified.
test_expectations: The two earlier negative mutations that removed nuw or nsw from affine_const's next increment now intentionally succeed; removal of both, and analogous add/sub/mul/shl cases, are positive one-way refinement tests. This does not permit added flags: unflagged-source to flagged-output mutations remain rejected, as do added FP/exact flags, opcode/type/operand changes, predicate/branch/successor changes and moved instructions. All earlier metadata/prefix/comment/split-line/placement and compact forwarding fixtures remain. Mutations cover guards on one or both sides, entry/count boundaries, shift amounts, constants, operands, widths, SSA uniqueness, block placement, argument widths, dominance, added flags and false count aliases. Every edge/width/constant in the other retained chains is mutated. Renamed early-exit siblings still reject n/span/limit/fake aliases; affine compaction rejects full-trip witnesses and an inverted empty guard. The original affine lit now explicitly checks the observed unflagged span and linked consumer count chain after ordinary LV, including repeated LV. Selected/Rejected, stage VF, scratch and executable semantic expectations are retained; no correctness check or trial was removed.

prior_validation.execution_failure: affine_runtime preheader %span = shl nuw nsw i64 %n, 1 became shl i64 %n, 1

diagnosis.status: Source-derived compiler path checked against immutable retained IR; no worker compiler invocation or instrumented trace.
diagnosis.observed_failure: affine_runtime preserves shl opcode, i64 width, %n/1 operands and preheader placement while removing nuw/nsw. Its consumer initializes AVL from a checked add/lshr/add expression instead of n or completed.count.
compiler_path: Ordinary consumer vectorization uses LoopVectorizationPlanner::executePlan with no vectorized epilogue, so expandSCEVsToVPInstructions runs before the classic late SCEVExpander fallback.

VPSCEVExpander::tryToExpand recursively expands the supported add/mul/udiv expression for the count. ScalarEvolution maps constant shl %n,1 to the 2*n mul SCEV; tryToReuseIRValue finds the preserved dominating %span in getSCEVValues.

canReuseInstruction first asks programUndefinedIfPoison. The span's poison would affect the eventual latch compare, but the forward scan stops at the producer's conditional diamond rather than proving UB across it. The reusable SCEV only propagates %n; the flags are extra poison contributors. The constant in-range shl creates no poison without flags, so canReuseInstruction collects it for flag removal.

VPSCEVExpander::tryToReuseIRValue directly invokes SCEVExpander::dropPoisonGeneratingAnnotationsAndReinfer on that existing IR instruction. The static helper drops flags. Reinference accepts only add/sub/mul and returns without restoring shift flags. Thus classic expandCodeFor/hoistIVInc need not be assumed to explain the removal.
diagnosis.subsequent_visible_counts: The same immutable LV1 output already contains unsigned umin/udiv, signed smax, signed descending smin, current-IV and enclosing-hoisted chains. Their narrow templates and original-control certificates are included now, rather than accepting arbitrary SSA counts or waiting for a known next assertion.
diagnosis.repair: One-way verified integer flag removal plus bounded, definition/width/block/edge-checked count provenance. Keep actual-completed and participant proofs separate from storage bounds.
diagnosis.expected_outcome: The retained nowrap/count mismatches should cease blocking the production checker, while mutations remain rejected. Fresh mandatory checks may expose a different later issue; no unobserved result is claimed.
